mainTopic: Answers to רבי יוחנן's contradiction about רבי יהודה and the egg, and the ברייתא about a doubtful or mixed egg, leading to the dispute about counted items and רב פפא's answer
overview: On the previous amud, רבי יוחנן found a contradiction in רבי יהודה's view about an egg laid on ראש השנה, and he answered by reversing the opinions. Here רבינא keeps the opinions as they are. He says רבי יהודה permits the egg even on the first day, and he only argued 'שתי קדושות' according to the רבנן's own view. The רבנן answered that the two days are קדושה אחת. רבינא בריה דרב עולא gives another answer: the hen was kept for laying eggs, so the egg is מוקצה, and רבי יהודה holds of מוקצה. Next the גמרא quotes a ברייתא that forbids moving such an egg and forbids even a doubtful egg. That strict ruling on a doubt fits רבה (הכנה, a Torah law) but is hard for רב יוסף and רבי יצחק (a rabbinic גזירה). The גמרא answers that the doubt is a ספק טרפה. It then asks why such an egg is not nullified when it is mixed into a thousand eggs. This leads to the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש over whether 'counted' items are significant. רב פפא answers that the ברייתא follows the תנא of ליטרא קציעות, and the גמרא begins quoting that משנה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבינא: Do not reverse the opinions
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers רבי יוחנן's contradiction without reversing the opinions. He says רבי יהודה was arguing according to the רבנן's view, not stating his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Really, do not reverse the opinions. רבי יהודה was speaking to the רבנן according to their own view.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a new way to solve רבי יוחנן's contradiction. He keeps the ברייתא as it is written and does not reverse the opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן had to reverse the opinions because רבי יהודה seemed to forbid the egg on the first day. רבינא says רבי יהודה never forbade it himself. He was only saying: 'Even by your own reasoning, you should permit it on the second day.' That removes the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (introduces the true explanation)
Do not reverse (the opinions)
According to their words / their view

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה changed his opinion here. He is only arguing from the רבנן's position to show that, even by their logic, the second day should be permitted.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Actually, do not reverse (the opinions),
phrases.notes: The גמרא is turning down רבי יוחנן's idea of switching the opinions.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda was speaking to them according to the words of the Rabbis:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative to רבי יוחנן's 'reverse the opinions' answer earlier.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the speaker's intent (arguing according to the opponent's view)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה forbids the egg on the first day, which contradicts his view that אוכלא דאפרת is permitted, so the opinions must be reversed.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה permits the egg even on the first day. His statement about the second day was only argued according to the רבנן's view.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's argument: at least permit it on the second day
steps.stepSummary: רבינא spells out what רבי יהודה meant. He permits the egg even on day one because it is אוכלא דאפרת. But even by the רבנן's view, they should permit it on day two, because the two days are שתי קדושות.
steps.simpleTranslation: In my view, it is permitted even on the first day, because it is food that separated from food. But according to your view, at least agree with me that it is permitted on the second day, because they are two separate sanctities.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in רבי יהודה's actual words to the רבנן, as רבינא understands them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה gives two levels. His own view is that the egg is permitted on day one, because it is like food that simply came out of food. His fallback argument, using the רבנן's view, is that day two is a separate day of קדושה, so what was forbidden on day one should be allowed on day two.

keyTerms.meaning: According to me / in my view
Food that separated (from other food), like an egg from an edible hen
According to you (plural)
At least agree with me
Two separate sanctities (the two days are independent)

steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whether the two days of ראש השנה are שתי קדושות or קדושה אחת becomes an important theme for laws that carry over from one day to the next.

phrases.english: According to me, even on the first day it is also permitted,
since it is food that separated (from food).
But according to you —
at least agree with me that on the second day it is permitted,
since they are two (separate) sanctities.
phrases.notes: The two days of ראש השנה are treated as separate units

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the content of רבינא's answer from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two-level argument (own view versus fallback argument from the opponent's view)
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה's mention of the second day is only a fallback argument, so it does not show that he forbids the egg on day one.

steps.title: The רבנן reply: the two days are one sanctity
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reject רבי יהודה's fallback argument. They hold that the two days of ראש השנה are קדושה אחת, so an egg forbidden on day one stays forbidden on day two.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן said to him: No, they are one sanctity.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside רבינא's version of the dispute, the רבנן answer רבי יהודה and refuse his 'two separate days' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the two days count as one long day of קדושה, then whatever was forbidden on day one is still forbidden on day two. That explains why the רבנן forbid the egg on both days. The ברייתא now reads smoothly with no reversal needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And they said to him
One sanctity (the two days are one continuous unit)

steps.whatToRemember: רבינא's answer: רבי יהודה permits the egg even on day one (אוכלא דאפרת). He only argued 'שתי קדושות' to persuade the רבנן, and they answered 'קדושה אחת'.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis said to him:
No, it is one sanctity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן: לָא, קְדוּשָּׁה אַחַת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The רבנן's response to רבי יהודה's argument in step 2, which completes רבינא's reading.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only רבי יהודה's fallback argument that day two is separate, within the reconstructed dispute.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument assumes the two days are שתי קדושות, but the רבנן hold they are קדושה אחת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With this reading, the ברייתא is consistent with רבי יהודה's view, and no reversal is needed.

steps.title: רבינא son of רב עולא: a hen kept for laying eggs
steps.stepSummary: רבינא בריה דרב עולא gives another answer. The egg in the ברייתא comes from a hen kept for laying eggs, not for eating. So the egg is מוקצה, and רבי יהודה holds that מוקצה is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא son of רב עולא said: Here we are dealing with a hen that is kept to produce eggs. רבי יהודה follows his usual reasoning, since he holds of מוקצה.
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא offers a second way to solve רבי יוחנן's contradiction, again without reversing the opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of אוכלא דאפרת only works when the hen itself counts as food. A hen kept for laying eggs is not set aside for eating, so it is מוקצה, and an egg coming from it is מוקצה too. רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה, therefore forbids the egg on day one, and there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: A hen kept for producing eggs (not for eating)
Following his own (usual) reasoning
Set aside, so it may not be used or moved on שבת or יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same person as the רבינא in step 1. This is רבינא בריה דרב עולא, giving a completely different answer.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that אוכלא דאפרת depends on the source being food. When the source is מוקצה, the product is treated as מוקצה too.

phrases.english: Ravina son of Rav Ulla said:
Here (we are dealing) with a hen kept for producing eggs,
and Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning,
since he holds of (the prohibition of) muktzeh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second alternative to רבי יוחנן's reversal, separate from רבינא's answer in steps 1 through 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא speaks of an ordinary egg from a food hen, so forbidding it on day one contradicts רבי יהודה's view on אוכלא דאפרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of a hen kept for eggs. The egg is מוקצה, and רבי יהודה forbids מוקצה, which fits his known view.

steps.title: Objection from a ברייתא: an egg laid on שבת or יום טוב may not be moved at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a challenge. It says an egg laid on שבת or on יום טוב may not be moved, not even to cover a vessel or to prop up a bed leg.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Both an egg laid on שבת and an egg laid on יום טוב may not be moved, neither to cover a vessel with it nor to support the legs of a bed with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge (מיתיבי) by quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the objection, and the full force of the challenge comes in the continuation of the ברייתא next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the egg as fully מוקצה, so it cannot be moved for any use, even a non-food one. It makes no difference whether the egg was laid on שבת or on יום טוב. The גמרא will use the rest of this ברייתא to test the earlier explanations of why the egg is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not move
To cover a vessel with it
The legs of a bed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not treat this step as a finished argument. The ברייתא is only being quoted here, and the actual question the גמרא draws from it comes next.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Both an egg that was laid on Shabbat
and an egg that was laid on Yom Tov —
one may not move it,
neither to cover a vessel with it,
nor to support the legs of a bed with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge from a ברייתא, and its full point continues next.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רב יוסף and רבי יצחק that the egg is forbidden only because of a rabbinic גזירה. Step 8 makes this explicit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats the egg as completely מוקצה, forbidden to move for any purpose, on both שבת and יום טוב. The גמרא will test which explanation of the egg's prohibition fits this ruling.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: covering the egg, a doubtful egg, and a mixed egg
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. You may cover the egg with a vessel so it does not break. A doubtful egg is forbidden. If the egg is mixed into a thousand eggs, all of them are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one may turn a vessel over on top of it so that it does not break. And a doubtful egg is forbidden. And if it got mixed into a thousand, they are all forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its quote of the ברייתא it began in Step 5. This step sets up the next move: the line about a doubtful egg is what the גמרא will question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may not move the egg itself, but you may move a vessel to protect it. The key new piece is that even when we are unsure whether the egg was laid on יום טוב, it is still forbidden. That is a strict ruling on a doubt, and the גמרא will now ask whose view it fits.

keyTerms.meaning: Turns a vessel upside down over it to cover it
It will break
A doubt; here, an egg we are unsure about
It got mixed into a thousand others

phrases.english: But one may turn a vessel over on it
phrases.notes: He moves the vessel, not the egg.

phrases.english: so that it does not break.
And a doubtful one is forbidden,
phrases.notes: At this point it's read as an egg we're not sure was laid on יום טוב.

phrases.english: and if it got mixed into a thousand,
they are all forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל כּוֹפֶה עָלֶיהָ אֶת הַכְּלִי בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא תִּשָּׁבֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: Sets up the challenge to רב יוסף and רבי יצחק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא rules strictly on a doubtful egg, which the next steps will test against each view.

steps.title: For רבה the strict ruling makes sense
steps.stepSummary: רבה holds the egg is forbidden because of הכנה, which is a Torah law. A doubt about a Torah law is treated strictly, so the ברייתא fits him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבה, who said the reason is הכנה. Then this is a Torah-level doubt, and every Torah-level doubt is treated strictly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the ברייתא fits רבה's view. This is the first half of a setup; the real question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה, the ban on the egg comes from the Torah, through the idea of הכנה. The rule is ספיקא דאורייתא לחומרא: when unsure about a Torah law, be strict. So forbidding a doubtful egg is exactly what רבה would expect.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for, this is fine for
Preparation; the Torah idea that food used on יום טוב must be ready beforehand
A doubt about a Torah law is treated strictly

phrases.english: It works well for Rabba,
who said it is because of preparation,
then it is a Torah-level doubt,
and every Torah-level doubt is treated strictly.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (first half of a בשלמא/אלא challenge)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the ברייתא's strict ruling on a doubt fits רבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבה, the egg's ban is from the Torah, so a doubt about it is treated strictly.

steps.title: For רב יוסף and רבי יצחק the strict ruling is a problem
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף and רבי יצחק hold the egg is forbidden only because of a rabbinic גזירה. A doubt about a rabbinic law is treated leniently, so the doubtful egg should be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for רב יוסף and רבי יצחק, who say the reason is a rabbinic decree, this is a rabbinic doubt. And every rabbinic doubt is treated leniently!
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the actual challenge. The ברייתא forbids a doubtful egg, but under these two views it should be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two אמוראים hold the egg's ban is only a rabbinic גזירה, not a Torah law. The rule is ספיקא דרבנן לקולא: when unsure about a rabbinic law, be lenient. So the ברייתא's strict ruling seems to contradict their view.

keyTerms.meaning: But (introduces the side with the problem)
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
A doubt about a rabbinic law is treated leniently

phrases.english: But according to Rav Yosef and Rabbi Yitzchak,
who say it is because of a decree,
it is a rabbinic doubt,
and every rabbinic doubt is treated leniently!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַב יוֹסֵף וּלְרַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּאָמְרִי מִשּׁוּם גְּזֵרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא/אלא pattern by showing whom the ברייתא is hard for.
steps.kashyaTarget: The views of רב יוסף and רבי יצחק that the egg is forbidden only by a rabbinic גזירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic ban means a doubt should be lenient, yet the ברייתא forbids the doubtful egg.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא is about a doubtful טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא is not about whether the egg was laid on יום טוב. It is about an egg from a hen that may be a טרפה, which is a Torah-level doubt, so it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: In the last part of the ברייתא, we have come to a case of a doubtful טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying the end of the ברייתא is talking about a different kind of doubt. That doubt is from the Torah, so the strict ruling fits everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubt is whether the hen that laid the egg is a טרפה, an animal with a fatal defect. An egg from a טרפה is forbidden by Torah law. So this is a ספיקא דאורייתא, and being strict is correct even for רב יוסף and רבי יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a text
We have come to (a different case)
A doubt whether the animal is a טרפה, one with a fatal defect

steps.whatToRemember: The answer here is that the end of the ברייתא is about a ספק טרפה, a Torah-level doubt, so being strict fits רבה, רב יוסף, and רבי יצחק alike. The גמרא immediately challenges this answer from the line 'mixed into a thousand' (Steps 10–11).
steps.confusionAlert: The doubt is not about the day the egg was laid. It is about the hen: is it a טרפה or not? Once you see that, the problem goes away.

phrases.english: (He said to him:)
In the last part, we have come to a doubtful tereifa.
phrases.notes: The hen may be a טרפה, which makes its egg forbidden by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 8 by redefining the case in the end of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) of the end of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the doubt was whether the egg was laid on יום טוב, a rabbinic doubt for רב יוסף and רבי יצחק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubt is whether the hen is a טרפה, a Torah-level doubt, so the strict ruling fits all views.

steps.title: The last line of the ברייתא fits only an egg that might be from יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the סיפא of the ברייתא: an egg mixed into a thousand makes them all forbidden. It explains why this works well if the doubt is about יום טוב: such an egg is a דבר שיש לו מתירין, and that is never nullified, even in a thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the last part of the ברייתא: 'If it got mixed into a thousand eggs, all of them are forbidden.' This makes sense if the doubt is whether the egg was laid on יום טוב or on a weekday. Then the egg will become permitted later on its own, and anything that will become permitted later is not cancelled out, even among a thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new challenge to the answer from Step 9 by quoting the last line of the ברייתא. This step sets up the attack: it first shows which reading of the ברייתא fits that line well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a forbidden item that gets mixed into many permitted items is cancelled out (בטל). But an item that will soon become permitted by itself (דבר שיש לו מתירין) is never cancelled, because you can simply wait. An egg that might be from יום טוב will be fine after יום טוב, so 'all are forbidden' fits that reading perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your answer is correct)
Say (look at) the last clause of the source
It became mixed in
An item that will become permitted later on its own
Nullified, cancelled out within a mixture

steps.confusionAlert: דבר שיש לו מתירין does not mean the egg is permitted now. It means the egg will become permitted later, after יום טוב. That is exactly why we do not cancel it: we can just wait.

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:
If it became mixed into a thousand, they are all forbidden.
phrases.notes: Quoting the end of the ברייתא from Step 6.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that there is a doubt whether it was laid on יום טוב or on a weekday,
then it is an item that will become permitted later,
phrases.notes: After יום טוב the egg will be permitted.

phrases.english: and any item that will become permitted later
is not nullified even in a thousand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new attack on the answer from Step 9 by bringing the last line of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 9 that the doubtful egg is a ספק טרפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'all are forbidden in a thousand' rule fits only an item that will become permitted later. That points to a ספק יום טוב egg, not a ספק טרפה egg.

steps.title: A doubtful טרפה egg should be nullified by a majority
steps.stepSummary: If the egg is a ספק טרפה, it will never become permitted. It is a דבר שאין לו מתירין, so it should be nullified by a simple majority, and the ברייתא should not forbid the whole mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say the egg is a doubtful טרפה egg, it is something that will never become permitted. So it should simply be cancelled out by the majority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lands the challenge. If the egg is a ספק טרפה, the ברייתא's ruling that all thousand eggs are forbidden does not make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טרפה egg stays forbidden forever, so there is no 'waiting' option. For such items the normal rule applies: a forbidden item in a mixture is cancelled by the majority (ביטול ברוב). The answer from Step 9 therefore clashes with the last line of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt whether the hen was a טרפה (fatally injured, forbidden)
An item that will never become permitted
So let it be nullified by the majority

phrases.english: But if you say it is a doubtful טרפה,
it is an item that will never become permitted,
so it should be nullified by a majority!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'בשלמא ... אלא' structure begun in Step 10. Step 10 showed what fits, and this step shows what does not.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of Step 9 (ספק טרפה) for רב יוסף and רבי יצחק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ספק טרפה egg is a דבר שאין לו מתירין and should be בטל ברוב. Yet the ברייתא forbids all thousand eggs, so the answer cannot be right.

steps.title: Suggested answer: an egg is important and cannot be nullified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that an egg is a 'significant' item (חשובה), and significant items are not nullified. This works according to the view that anything that is sometimes counted, like an egg, counts as significant (כל שדרכו לימנות).
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that an egg is an important item and so it is not cancelled out, that works well for the one who says the rule is 'anything that is sometimes sold by count.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible defense of the ספק טרפה answer: an egg is too important to be cancelled. It notes right away that this works only according to one opinion, which sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some items are so important that they are never cancelled in a mixture. The test is whether the item is sold by count. According to the view 'כל שדרכו לימנות', it is enough that eggs are sometimes sold by count, so an egg qualifies.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible answer)
Significant, important (so it cannot be nullified)
That works well according to the one who says
Anything whose way is (even sometimes) to be counted

steps.confusionAlert: Pay attention to the tiny difference in wording: 'כל' (anything, even sometimes counted) versus 'את' (only that which is always counted). The whole argument hangs on this one word.

phrases.english: And if you say
that an egg is significant and is not nullified,
that works well according to the one who said:
'Anything whose way is to be counted' is what we learned.
phrases.notes: Eggs are sometimes sold by count, so they qualify.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא בֵּיצָה חֲשׁוּבָה וְלֹא בָּטְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense against the challenge in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a separate reason the egg is not nullified: it is important (חשובה), regardless of whether it is a דבר שיש לו מתירין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ספק טרפה egg must be nullified by a majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: An egg is a counted item, and important items are never nullified. This holds at least according to the view 'כל שדרכו לימנות'.

steps.title: The suggested answer fails for the view that only always-counted items are important
steps.stepSummary: According to the view 'את שדרכו לימנות', only items that are always sold by count are significant. Eggs are not always sold by count, so they would be nullified, and the challenge to the ספק טרפה answer remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says the rule is 'that which is always sold by count,' what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the 'important egg' answer does not work for everyone. The question against the ספק טרפה answer returns, and רב פפא answers it in Step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to 'את שדרכו לימנות', an item counts as important only if it is always sold by count. Eggs are often sold by weight or volume too, so they are not important and should be nullified. The ספק טרפה answer is again in trouble according to this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Only that which is always sold by count
What can be said? (a pointed challenge; Step 18 answers it)

steps.whatToRemember: The ספק טרפה answer explains why the doubtful egg is forbidden, but it struggles with the line 'all are forbidden in a thousand.' Only a ספק יום טוב egg (דבר שיש לו מתירין) clearly fits that line. The 'important egg' defense works only according to 'כל שדרכו לימנות', not according to 'את שדרכו לימנות'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows two separate reasons an item may escape nullification: דבר שיש לו מתירין, and being a counted, significant item. Both concepts appear across all of איסור והיתר.

phrases.english: But according to the one who said:
'That which is always counted' is what we learned,
phrases.notes: Eggs are not always sold by count.

phrases.english: what can be said?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: אֶת שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לִימָּנוֹת שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the defense in Step 12 by showing that it fails according to the other opinion, which brings back the challenge of Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The defense in Step 12 that an egg is חשובה and cannot be nullified.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to 'את שדרכו לימנות', an egg is not always counted, so it is not significant. It should therefore be nullified by a majority, and the ספק טרפה reading again cannot explain 'all are forbidden.'

steps.title: The משנה of the fenugreek bundles from a vineyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the משנה where the dispute about 'significant items' comes from. רבי מאיר says mixed-in bundles of forbidden fenugreek forbid everything. חכמים say they are nullified in 1 part to 200.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If someone had bundles of fenugreek that grew as כלאי הכרם, they must be burned. If they got mixed with other bundles, and those got mixed with still others, all of them must be burned. This is the view of רבי מאיר. חכמים say: they are nullified if there is one forbidden part against two hundred permitted parts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing the source משנה behind the two views it mentioned in steps 12–13. This sets up the next lines, which explain the reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כלאי הכרם is forbidden for any benefit, so the forbidden bundles must be burned. רבי מאיר says that even after they get mixed in, nothing is nullified and everything must be burned. חכמים say the normal rule for כלאי הכרם applies: it is nullified in 1 against 200.

keyTerms.meaning: Bundles of fenugreek (a legume plant)
Forbidden mixed crops grown in a vineyard; no benefit may be taken from them
They must be burned
They are nullified in a ratio of one forbidden part to two hundred permitted parts

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
One who had bundles of fenugreek
that were mixed crops of the vineyard — they must be burned.
phrases.notes: כלאי הכרם are forbidden for any benefit, so they are destroyed by burning.

phrases.english: If they got mixed with others, and those others with still others —
all of them must be burned; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say: they are nullified in one part to two hundred.
phrases.notes: That is, one forbidden part among 200 permitted parts (201 total).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the two views about significant items mentioned in steps 12–13.
steps.raayaObject: The existence of the dispute about which items are significant and not nullified.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in ערלה 3:6 about fenugreek bundles of כלאי הכרם.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's reason and the list of special items
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains רבי מאיר's reason: anything normally counted forbids the whole mixture. חכמים limit this to six specific items, and רבי עקיבא adds a seventh. These items forbid the mixture under ערלה or כלאי הכרם, whichever applies to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר used to say: something that is normally sold by count forbids the whole mixture. חכמים say only six items forbid the mixture. רבי עקיבא says seven. They are: nuts of Perekh, pomegranates of Badan, sealed barrels, leaves of beets, cabbage stalks, and Greek gourds. רבי עקיבא adds homeowners' loaves of bread. Whichever item can be ערלה is forbidden as ערלה, and whichever item can be כלאי הכרם is forbidden as כלאי הכרם.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and explains why רבי מאיר forbids everything. Items that are counted are 'significant' and never get nullified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר gives a broad rule based on counting. חכמים do not accept a broad rule and only allow a fixed list of six (or seven) important items. The closing lines explain that each item on the list is forbidden by whichever prohibition fits it: fruits by ערלה, vegetables by כלאי הכרם.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: makes the whole mixture forbidden (not 'sanctifies')
That which is normally sold by count
Sealed barrels (of wine)
Loaves baked by a homeowner (large, important loaves)
Fruit from a tree's first three years, forbidden for benefit

steps.confusionAlert: The word מקדש here does not mean 'makes holy.' It means the forbidden item makes the whole mixture forbidden. Also, notice the wording 'את שדרכו לימנות.' That exact wording is what רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about in the next step.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Meir used to say:
That which is normally counted — makes the mixture forbidden;
And the Sages say: nothing makes the mixture forbidden
except six items only;
Rabbi Akiva says: seven.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: אֱגוֹזֵי פֶּרֶךְ, וְרִמּוֹנֵי בָּאדָן,
phrases.english: And these are they: nuts of Perekh, and pomegranates of Badan,
and sealed barrels, and leaves of beets,
and cabbage stalks, and Greek gourd.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מוֹסִיף אַף כִּכָּרוֹת שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva adds: also loaves of a homeowner.
That which can be orlah — is forbidden as orlah.
That which can be kilei hakerem — is forbidden as kilei hakerem.
phrases.notes: Vegetables like beets, cabbage, and gourds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה and gives the reasoning behind רבי מאיר's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, items normally sold by count are significant and forbid a mixture. According to חכמים, only six (or seven) listed items do.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about the wording
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה's text is 'את שדרכו לימנות': only things always sold by count. ריש לקיש says it reads 'כל שדרכו לימנות': anything that is sometimes sold by count.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said about this משנה: רבי יוחנן said, 'We learned את שדרכו לימנות, that which is always counted.' ריש לקיש said, 'We learned כל שדרכו לימנות, anything that is sometimes counted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the argument between two אמוראים about the exact wording of רבי מאיר's rule. These are the two views that steps 12–13 depended on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference of one word changes how wide the rule is. 'את' limits it to items that are always sold by count. 'כל' includes items that are only sometimes counted, like eggs. So an egg is significant according to ריש לקיש but not according to רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was said about it (an אמורא statement on the משנה)
Anything that is sometimes sold by count

steps.whyThisMatters: This argument decides whether an egg counts as significant. That is the key to whether the ספק טרפה answer can explain why the egg is not nullified even in a thousand.

phrases.english: And it was stated about it:
Rabbi Yochanan said:
We learned 'that which is (always) counted.'
And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
We learned 'anything that is (sometimes) counted.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the אמוראים' dispute over the wording of the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: only items always sold by count are significant. ריש לקיש: even items sometimes sold by count are significant.

steps.title: The challenge returns: what about רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: Having brought the source, the גמרא repeats its challenge. Saying the egg is significant works for ריש לקיש. According to רבי יוחנן, an egg is not significant, so a ספק טרפה egg should be nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to ריש לקיש. But according to רבי יוחנן, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the egg and presses its challenge again, now that the source is clear. The ספק טרפה explanation still seems to fail according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, an egg is sometimes counted, so it is significant and is not nullified even in a thousand. According to רבי יוחנן, eggs are not always counted, so they are not significant. A ספק טרפה egg is a דבר שאין לו מתירין, so it should be nullified by a simple majority. That contradicts the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (according to one view)
What can be said? (a challenge to this view; the next step answers it)

steps.whatToRemember: The answer that the end of the ברייתא is about a ספק טרפה egg fits ריש לקיש (כל שדרכו לימנות), because for him an egg is significant. According to רבי יוחנן (את שדרכו לימנות), the גמרא asks why the egg is not nullified. רב פפא answers this in the next step.

phrases.english: This works well according to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן — מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?
phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Yochanan — what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the source citation, returns to the challenge of step 13 and restates it explicitly.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 9 that the end of the ברייתא is about a ספק טרפה egg.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי יוחנן, an egg is not significant. A ספק טרפה egg is a דבר שאין לו מתירין, so it should be nullified by a majority, yet the ברייתא forbids even a thousand.

steps.title: The egg ruling follows the תנא of the pressed figs
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the egg ruling follows the תנא of ליטרא קציעות. That תנא holds that any counted item is never nullified, even for a rabbinic prohibition, and certainly not for a Torah prohibition like טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This תנא is the תנא of the 'litra of dried figs.' He says that anything that is counted is not nullified, even for a rabbinic prohibition. All the more so it is not nullified for a Torah prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question from step 17. He says the egg ruling does not have to fit the view of רבי יוחנן's reading of the dispute. It follows a different תנא who holds a wider rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that according to רבי יוחנן, an egg is not 'significant' and should be nullified. רב פפא answers that the egg ruling follows the תנא of ליטרא קציעות, who says any counted item is never nullified. He argues with a קל וחומר: if this holds for a rabbinic prohibition, it surely holds for a Torah prohibition like a טרפה egg.

keyTerms.meaning: A litra (a weight measure) of dried, pressed figs
An item that is counted (sold by number), so it is considered significant
Is nullified (loses its identity in a mixture)
All the more so (a קל וחומר)

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not changing what רבי יוחנן said about the other משנה. He is saying the egg ruling comes from a different תנא with a wider rule, so רבי יוחנן's reading does not create a problem.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the ספק טרפה explanation for the egg according to both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This Tanna (who rules the egg is not nullified)
is the Tanna of the 'litra of dried figs,'
who says: any item that is counted,
even for a rabbinic prohibition, is not nullified,
and all the more so for a Torah prohibition.
phrases.notes: Like a טרפה egg, which is a Torah prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַאי תַּנָּא — תַּנָּא דְּלִיטְרָא קְצִיעוֹת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 17 according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the ruling to a different תנא with a broader rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to רבי יוחנן, an egg is not significant, so a ספק טרפה egg should be nullified.
steps.terutzMaskana: The egg ruling follows the תנא of ליטרא קציעות. For him, any counted item is never nullified, even for a rabbinic prohibition and surely for a Torah one.

steps.title: The משנה of the pressed figs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a litra of figs pressed onto one of several vessels, where the person does not know which one. רבי מאיר begins reporting a dispute starting with רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Someone had a litra of dried figs and pressed it onto the mouth of a round vessel, but he does not know which round vessel he pressed it onto. Or he pressed it onto the mouth of a barrel, but does not know which barrel. Or he pressed it onto the mouth of a hive-shaped container, but does not know which one. רבי מאיר says: רבי אליעזר...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings the source for רב פפא's claim by quoting the ליטרא קציעות משנה. This passage stops in the middle, just as רבי מאיר starts telling us רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the figs are forbidden only by rabbinic law, and they got mixed in among several containers. The three cases (round vessel, barrel, hive) are the same idea: the forbidden figs are somewhere in a group and we do not know where. The dispute that comes next will show which תנא holds that counted items are not nullified, which is the source for רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: He pressed it (the figs)
A round vessel or mold for pressing figs into a cake
A barrel
A hive-shaped straw container

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishnah:
A litra of dried figs
that he pressed onto the mouth of a round vessel,
and he does not know onto which round vessel he pressed it;
or onto the mouth of a barrel,
and he does not know onto which barrel he pressed it;
or onto the mouth of a hive-shaped container,
and he does not know onto which container he pressed it.
Rabbi Meir says: Rabbi Eliezer...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud. רבי מאיר is reporting a dispute between earlier תנאים.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: לִיטְרָא קְצִיעוֹת שֶׁדְּרָסָהּ עַל פִּי עִגּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the משנה that supports רב פפא's claim in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that there is a תנא who holds that counted items are never nullified, even for a rabbinic prohibition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of ליטרא קציעות (figs pressed onto an unknown vessel), with the dispute reported by רבי מאיר.
